d: Role Description The Director role at Techcombank is a full-time, on-site position based in Thủ Đức. The Director will provide strategic leadership for a designated business or functional area, setting vision, defining priorities, and ensuring alignment with the bank’s digital, data, and talent strategy. This role oversees the development and execution of business plans, manages budgets and performance targets, and ensures compliance with internal policies and regulatory requirements. The Director will lead and develop high-performing teams, foster collaboration across departments, and drive initiatives that enhance customer experience and operational efficiency. Day-to-day responsibilities include stakeholder management, decision-making on key projects, risk assessment, and continuous improvement of processes and services to support sustainable growth.
q: Strong leadership, people management, and team development skills, with experience guiding diverse, high-performing teams.
Strategic planning and business management capabilities, including setting objectives, managing budgets, and measuring performance.
Experience in banking or financial services, with solid understanding of products, operations, risk, and regulatory environments.
Ability to drive digital and data-enabled transformation, including process optimization, customer experience enhancement, and use of analytics.
Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence at senior levels.
Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and analytical skills, with a track record of delivering complex projects or initiatives.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Management, or a related field; a master’s degree or relevant professional certification is an advantage.
High level of integrity, resilience, and adaptability, with commitment to inclusive, non-discriminatory workplace practices.

d: Location Al Shuhada Street, P.O.Box 1216, Kuwait City 15463, KuwaitVIEW ON MAP

Respond and attend to guest repair requests. Communicate with guests/customers to resolve maintenance issues. Perform preventive maintenance on tools and kitchen and mechanical room equipment, including cleaning and lubrication. Visually inspect tools, equipment, or machines. Carry equipment (e.g., tools, radio). Identify, locate, and operate all shut-off valves for equipment and all utility shut-offs for buildings. Maintain maintenance inventory and requisition parts and supplies as needed. Communicate each day’s activities and problems that occur to the other shifts using approved communication programs and standards. Display basic knowledge or ability to acquire knowledge in the following categories: air conditioning and refrigeration, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, pneumatic/electronic systems and controls, carpentry and finish skills, kitchen equipment, vehicles, energy conservation, and/or general building. Perform all surface preparation, painting, minor drywall and wood trim repair, light bulb and A/C filter replacement and the complete and thorough cleanup of the painting or repair area. Test, troubleshoot and perform basic repair on all types of equipment, plumbing (e.g., plunge toilets and unclog drains), electrical components including lamps, cosmetic items, extension cords, vacuum cleaners, internet devices, replace electrical switches and outlets, and other guestroom items. Program TV's and perform general housekeeping and engineering-related inventory duties. Use the Lockout/Tagout system before performing any maintenance work. Perform repairs on interior and exterior landscaping as well as external landscaping sprinklers. Display basic computer skills including inputting air handler schedules and making temperature changes.

Follow all company and safety and security policies and procedures; report any maintenance problems, safety hazards, accidents, or injuries; complete safety training and certifications; and properly store flammable materials. Develop and maintain positive working relationships with others, support team to reach common goals, and listen and respond appropriately to the concerns of other employees. Speak with others using clear and professional language. Move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 50 pounds without assistance and heavier lifting or movement tasks with assistance. Move up and down stairs, service ramps, and/or ladders. Reach overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping. Enter and locate work-related information using computers. Perform other reasonable job duties as requested.
q: Education: High school diploma or G.E.D equivalent.
Related Work Experience: Some experience in general maintenance, exterior and interior surface preparation and painting.
Experience in hotel engineering or maintenance a plus.

d: CMC Markets Middle East Limited (CMCME) is seeking an AML/KYC Associate to join its Compliance – Financial Crime team in the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC).

Reporting to the Compliance Officer and MLRO, you will play an important role in implementing and maintaining the firm's anti-money laundering (AML), counter-terrorist financing (CFT), counter-proliferation financing (CPF) and sanctions framework. You will support compliance with the DFSA's AML requirements, applicable UAE federal legislation and Group policies.

This is a hands-on operational role suited to someone with practical experience in KYC, client onboarding or financial crime compliance who can manage a caseload independently and contribute from day one. CMCME serves Professional Clients, including corporate entities with complex ownership structures. You will therefore work across a range of due diligence requirements, from individual client verification to beneficial ownership analysis and source of wealth assessments.

Working closely with the Senior Compliance Analyst and the CO/MLRO, you will help ensure that client onboarding, ongoing monitoring and financial crime controls are completed accurately, efficiently and in line with regulatory expectations.
As you develop your expertise and demonstrate the required competence, you will have the opportunity to take on delegated authority for approving lower-risk client accounts.
q: Approximately 1–3 years’ KYC, onboarding or AML experience within a firm regulated by the DFSA, FSRA, SCA or FCA.
Working knowledge of the relevant AML/CFT and sanctions requirements (DFSA AML Module, FSRA AML Rulebook, SCA requirements or the UK Money Laundering Regulations and FCA rules).
Practical experience of corporate due diligence, including beneficial ownership analysis.
Experience assessing source of funds and source of wealth.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to spot inconsistencies in documents and information.
Clear written communication, including the ability to document decisions and rationale concisely.
Well organised, with the ability to manage a caseload and meet service levels.
Professional integrity and discretion in handling confidential information.
Direct experience of the DFSA AML Module.
Experience with trusts, foundations, family offices or other complex structures.
Familiarity with screening and verification tools, such as World-Check, Dow Jones, ComplyAdvantage or LexisNexis.
Experience in online trading, CFDs, brokerage, investment services, private banking or wealth management.
An AML qualification, such as the ICA Certificate in AML or CAMS, or progress towards one.
Degree in law, finance, business, economics, criminology or a related subject.
Arabic language skills, experience working in the DIFC and existing UAE residency.

CMC Markets is powered by our people. We are an equal opportunities employer and are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, where people feel confident to be themselves, feel valued and are able to do their best work.
The Company reserves the right to review, alter and amend this job description from time to time in line with business requirements.
r: Client Onboarding and Customer Due Diligence
Carry out the customer risk assessment at onboarding and assign a risk rating in line with CMCME’s methodology, using it to determine the level of due diligence required.

Carry out due diligence on corporate and other legal structures, including holding companies, SPVs, trusts, foundations and family offices, identifying and verifying beneficial owners, controllers and authorised signatories.
Verify the identity of individual clients and connected persons in line with CMCME’s CDD procedures.
Assess source of funds and source of wealth, and check that information obtained is consistent with the client’s profile, business and expected activity.

Prepare enhanced due diligence files for higher-risk clients, including politically exposed persons and clients connected to higher-risk jurisdictions, for approval by the CO/MLRO and senior management.
Work with the Senior Compliance Analyst on Professional Client classification evidence gathered during onboarding.
Over time, and once competence has been demonstrated, approve lower-risk client accounts within delegated authority.
Liaise with clients, sales and operations teams to obtain outstanding information and documents.

Screen clients, beneficial owners and connected parties against sanctions lists (including the UAE Local Terrorist List, the UN Consolidated List and other lists applied by CMCME), PEP databases and adverse media.
Review and discount or escalate potential screening matches, documenting the rationale clearly.
Support CMCME’s procedures for implementing targeted financial sanctions without delay, including freezing measures and required notifications, under the direction of the CO/MLRO.
Carry out periodic KYC reviews in line with each client’s risk rating, and event-driven reviews where a client’s ownership, control or circumstances change.
Review transaction monitoring alerts and unusual activity, gathering information and documenting the outcome.
Check client deposits and withdrawals for third-party payments, name mismatches and funding patterns inconsistent with the client’s profile, working with the payments and operations teams.
Track expired documents and outstanding KYC items, and follow up to resolution.
Identify and promptly escalate potential suspicious activity to the CO/MLRO through internal reporting procedures.
Assist the CO/MLRO in gathering information and preparing reports submitted to the UAE Financial Intelligence Unit via goAML.
Maintain confidentiality and follow tipping-off requirements at all times.
Maintain the internal suspicious activity and FIU reporting registers.
Maintain complete, accurate and auditable CDD files and records in line with record-keeping requirements.
Prepare AML management information, including onboarding volumes, client risk profile, screening and alert statistics, and overdue reviews.
Assist the CO/MLRO in preparing the annual MLRO report and the annual DFSA AML Return.
Support the periodic update of CMCME’s business risk assessment for money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing.
Assist with DFSA supervisory requests, internal audits and external AML reviews.
Liaise with the Group MLRO and global Financial Crime teams, applying Group policies alongside local requirements.
Help keep AML/KYC procedures, checklists and templates up to date with regulatory and business change.
Monitor updates from the DFSA, the UAE FIU, the Executive Office for Control and Non-Proliferation, the National Anti-Money Laundering Committee and FATF, and flag relevant developments.
Support the delivery of AML/CFT and sanctions training to staff.
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of the DFSA AML Module, UAE AML/CFT and sanctions requirements, and financial crime typologies relevant to CMCME’s business.
Complete required training and continuing professional development.
Undertake other duties reasonably required for the role and consistent with its level of responsibility.

d: Manage governance committee operations and administration to ensure effective decision-making, compliance with governance frameworks, and the efficient execution of committee responsibilities.
Oversee committee governance processes, documentation, meeting management, action tracking, and stakeholder coordination while ensuring adherence to organizational policies and governance standards.
Support organizational governance effectiveness through robust committee management, reporting, and continuous improvement initiatives.
q: Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Corporate Governance, Law, Public Administration, Finance, Management, or a related field.
CGI/ICSA Governance Qualification, GRCP, PMP, or equivalent professional certification preferred.
6–10 years of experience in governance, corporate secretariat, committee management, compliance, executive administration, or related disciplines.
Managing governance committees, executive forums, or board-related activities.
Preparing governance documentation, committee submissions, minutes, and action trackers.
Supporting governance frameworks, policy implementation, and organizational governance initiatives.
Coordinating with senior executives, committee members, and business stakeholders.
Supporting governance audits, compliance reviews, and governance reporting activities.
r: Manage the planning, scheduling, and administration of governance committees and related governance forums.
Oversee the preparation, review, quality assurance, and distribution of committee agendas, reports, presentations, and supporting materials.
Ensure committee submissions comply with governance requirements, approval protocols, documentation standards, and established procedures.
Coordinate committee meetings and ensure timely circulation of meeting packs, resolutions, and governance communications.
Oversee the preparation and review of meeting minutes, action logs, decision registers, and governance records.
Monitor and track committee actions, decisions, and resolutions to ensure timely completion and accountability across business functions.
Provide governance advice and support to stakeholders regarding committee processes, documentation requirements, and governance expectations.
Maintain governance frameworks, committee charters, terms of reference, and governance documentation repositories.
Prepare governance reports, committee performance metrics, dashboards, and management updates for leadership review.
Identify governance risks, process gaps, and opportunities for improvement and recommend appropriate corrective actions.
Support governance audits, compliance reviews, and assurance activities related to committee operations and governance practices.
Lead and develop governance coordinators, analysts, or support staff while promoting governance best practices and continuous improvement.

d: Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat, where impact, innovation, and growth drives everything we do. Our Commercial team sits at the centre of Deliveroo’s marketplace - shaping how we serve restaurants, grocers, and new verticals worldwide. From negotiating key partnerships to unlocking new revenue streams and crafting data-led growth strategies, we take on big challenges that move the business forward. If you thrive in fast-paced, commercial environments and want to influence the future of a global brand - this is the team for you.

As Deliveroo continues to scale, we become a major revenue channel for restaurants - aside from providing best-in-class support, we are restaurant consultants that use data-driven insight and industry knowledge to help our partner restaurants grow. Our account management team owns and manages restaurant relationships. We are restaurant consultants who use data-driven analytics and industry knowledge to provide best-in-class support and strategic value to our restaurant partners. The Account Managers are a passionate, dynamic group of team players who work well together and cross-functionally with other departments, and of course, they’re fun, personable, and great at building exceptional relationships.

As an Account Manager, you will manage a portfolio of restaurant partners on Deliveroo, with a focus on high-performing Local Gems and selected national chains. These partners play an important role in attracting customers to the marketplace and represent strong growth opportunities for Deliveroo. You will work closely with your partners to improve operational performance, drive marketing initiatives, and identify opportunities to grow their business on the Deliveroo platform. You will also collaborate with internal teams across marketing, operations, and commercial functions to ensure partners deliver a strong customer experience while achieving sustainable growth.
q: Our ideal candidate will bring strong expertise in some of these areas and curiosity to grow in others:
Minimum of 3-5 years of experience in a commercial role in a fast-paced environment
Commercial mindset with the ability to identify growth opportunities
Very data-conversant with an ability to utilise and analyse data to tell a story
Great organisational skills with excellent team-player qualities
Strong relationship management and stakeholder engagement skills
Problem-solving mindset and ability to navigate operational challenges
Enjoy working in a constantly evolving environment
Demonstrate strong competency using Microsoft Office tools and related project/program management applications to drive best practices
Strong knowledge of the restaurant industry is a plus
Fluency in English and Arabic is a must
r: Manage a portfolio of Deliveroo's restaurants in Kuwait, including high-sales volume drivers and global restaurant brands. You will maintain and grow relationships with these partners.

Lead the delivery agenda with your partners to ensure they are operating with excellent fundamentals, and define and execute joint initiatives that drive sustainable growth for both Deliveroo and your partners.

Lead the day-to-day management of your accounts, interacting primarily with stakeholders who manage daily projects or operations. You will work on negotiations and longer-term account plans in collaboration with your Restaurant Partner.
Monitor operational metrics and support partners in improving service quality
Drive adoption of Deliveroo marketing tools, promotions, and campaigns
Support partner onboarding and expansion onto the Deliveroo platform
Demonstrate the ability to resolve day-to-day issues and problem-solve independently, seeking advice for more complex problems when necessary
Work cross-functionally with other departments (Marketing, Operations) to lead new projects and drive initiatives forward
x: At Deliveroo, you’ll do work that matters, solving real-world problems in a three-sided marketplace that’s constantly evolving.
